summary.text: Arachnids are arthropods of the class Arachnida, a group that includes spiders, scorpions, ticks, mites and harvestmen.
Almost all adult arachnids have eight legs, unlike adult insects, which have six, and arachnids have no antennae or wings.
Their body has two sections, a cephalothorax and an abdomen, and almost all living arachnids are terrestrial.

facts.label: First appendage pair
facts.value: The chelicerae, used in feeding and defense

facts.label: Scorpion stinger
facts.value: A telson modified into a stinger

items.prompt: You catch a small creature with eight legs, no antennae and no wings. Which describes it best?

options.label: An insect, since adult insects have eight legs
An arachnid, since adults have eight legs and lack antennae and wings
An insect, since all insects lack wings and antennae
A scorpion, since only scorpions have eight legs

items.explain: Almost all adult arachnids have eight legs, while adult insects have six, and arachnids have neither antennae nor wings.

items.prompt: The pinchers at the front of a scorpion are formed by which pair of appendages?

options.label: The pedipalps
The chelicerae
The pectines
The spinnerets

items.explain: In scorpions the pedipalps end in a pair of pinchers. The chelicerae are the first pair and serve in feeding and defense.

items.prompt: A desert arachnid loses very little water through its body. Which adaptation helps it?

options.label: Gills along the sides of its abdomen, which trap moisture
Wings that carry it between far-apart sources of water
A waxy layer over its cuticle and efficient excretory structures
Antennae that detect water from far across the sand

items.explain: Water conservation on land is aided by a waxy layer covering the cuticle and efficient excretory structures.

items.prompt: Most arachnids lack extensor muscles in the outer joints of their legs. How does a spider straighten its legs?

options.label: It tightens the cartilage-like tissue inside its body
It pulls its legs straight with elastic joints, as solifuges do
It relies on muscles that extend two joints at once
It uses the pressure of its body fluid to push the limbs out

items.explain: Spiders and whip scorpions extend their limbs hydraulically using the pressure of their hemolymph.

items.prompt: Under a microscope, a mite larva has only six legs. What would you usually expect after it moults into a nymph?

options.label: It loses its legs entirely
A fourth pair of legs usually appears
It grows a pair of antennae
It stays at six legs for life

items.explain: The larvae of mites have six legs, and a fourth pair usually appears when they moult into nymphs.

items.prompt: Why do some scientists question the name cephalothorax for the front section of an arachnid?

options.label: No fossil or embryo shows that a separate thorax-like division ever existed
The front section has no legs attached to it
The front section is covered by many separate plates
The front section is found only in scorpions

items.explain: The name implies a fused head and thorax, but there is neither fossil nor embryological evidence that arachnids ever had a separate thorax-like division.
